column3: The home declares its reads on defineOp ({read: true}) and ignores the client's read flag; the web read table moves to web/src/lib/reads.ts and a server test checks every entry is declared. Agent-side memory writes (remember, the Dreamer) bump the home revision through wire.announce(), so memory.list and memory.profile stay cached; automation.list stays cached because automation changes already publish a home snap
column4: Bosun and XIN-23: a client-declared read could hide a mutation, and agent writes reached cached memory and automation reads only through the 60 s TTL. Bumping costs 0 rows, so it beats making those reads live
column5: src/reads.test.ts: every web read is declared (no x-ingle-rev) and an agent remember moves the revision by one; src/cmd.test.ts: a mutation sent with read:true still bumps; web/src/lib/cmd.test.ts: drive reads are never cached
